segments.title: 第23章 改觀
segments.content:
Chapter 23 A Change of Perspective

Faced with Li Luo's greeting, Ying Zhicheng glanced at the boy's face, then at the clothes in his hands, and couldn't help but ask, "What are you doing?"

"Oh, me," Li Luo blinked, looking innocent. "Ying Chanxi called me at noon and said it was going to rain, so she asked me to help her bring in her clothes."

As he spoke, Li Luo had already walked to the door of Ying Chanxi's bedroom, opened it, and went inside.

After placing the clothes on her bed, he immediately came back out.

He didn't have anything to feel guilty about.

After all, Ying Zhicheng had practically watched him grow up. The two families could freely enter each other's homes, so it was perfectly normal for Ying Chanxi to ask him to collect her clothes.

Ying Zhicheng indeed didn't react much to this. After changing into another pair of slippers, he walked into the living room and asked Li Luo, "Xixi is still at school, right?"

"Yes."

"Today's Friday." Ying Zhicheng thought for a moment and said, "I remember she should be getting out of school a bit earlier?"

"Yes, there's no evening self-study on Fridays. Ying Chanxi usually gets home around five-thirty in the evening," Li Luo replied, wondering if he should make his escape.

Being alone in the living room with Uncle Ying was a little awkward.

Ying Zhicheng felt the same way, though he certainly wouldn't say it out loud. "I'm cooking a meal tonight. I've already spoken with your dad. Come over together in the evening to eat, let's have a get-together."

In truth, Ying Zhicheng didn't like Li Luo.

Of course, he couldn't say he disliked him either.

He and Li Guohong had been best buddies since they were young, and their relationship was excellent.

Naturally, he wouldn't reject his best friend's son.

It was just that this kid, Li Luo, was a bit too wild. Ying Zhicheng was always worried he would lead his own daughter astray.

Especially since he worked in the city long-term and usually had no time to look after Ying Chanxi.

If Ying Chanxi was led by Li Luo to fool around all day, her grades would definitely be affected.

But after a long time had passed, Ying Zhicheng discovered that his daughter's grades had always remained first in the entire school, never dropping, so he stopped worrying.

Coupled with the fact that his best friend's family lived right next door and often took care of his daughter, Ying Zhicheng didn't meddle anymore and focused on making money over there.

But regarding Li Luo, he just couldn't bring himself to like him.

And Li Luo could sense this, so he naturally wouldn't linger. After hearing what Ying Zhicheng said, he walked toward the door. "Then, Uncle Ying, I'll come back with my parents this evening to impose. I'm going back to catch up on sleep first."

"Alright." Ying Zhicheng took off his suit jacket. Seeing that he was about to leave, he suddenly asked again, "What does Xixi like to eat these days? Eggplant with minced pork?"

"Yes." Li Luo was changing his shoes at the door. Hearing this question, he immediately said, "Eggplant with minced pork, scrambled eggs with tomato, and cola chicken wings. Those are her three favorite dishes."

"She really hasn't changed at all." Ying Zhicheng shook his head with a chuckle.

"After all, they're the three dishes Auntie is best at making," Li Luo said with a smile after putting on his shoes. "I quite like them too."

"Hmm..." Ying Zhicheng fell silent and didn't respond further.

So Li Luo appropriately opened the door, preparing to go home.

But as soon as he opened it, Li Luo saw a delivery courier standing at his door, about to raise his hand to knock.

Knock, knock, knock.

"Anyone home? Your delivery is here!"

"Is that a delivery for 401?" Li Luo asked unexpectedly from behind the courier.

The courier was startled by the voice behind him. He turned to look at Li Luo, then glanced at the package in his hand. "Yeah, for 401. Do you know this family?"

"Of course I do, I live in 401." Li Luo walked out from the doorway of 402, took out his key, and opened the door to 401. "But I don't think my family ordered anything online. What are you delivering?"

"An admission notice." Seeing Li Luo open the door to 401, the courier handed him the package. "You must be Li Luo, right? Do you have an ID or student card? I need you to sign for confirmation."

"Oh, okay, please wait a moment." As Li Luo said this, he was thinking of closing the door to 402 first.

But just then, Ying Zhicheng from the living room had been drawn over by the sound and was standing at the door, asking curiously, "An admission notice?"

"Yes." Seeing that Ying Zhicheng had no intention of closing the door, Li Luo replied before heading back into his home to get his student card.

Ying Zhicheng, however, looked at the package with curiosity and couldn't help asking, "Which school's admission notice is it?"

"First Affiliated High, I think," the courier said casually. "Your neighbor's kid is pretty impressive, huh? I remember First Affiliated High is considered the best high school in our Yinjiang District, right?"

Hearing the courier's reply, Ying Zhicheng was clearly stunned for a moment, unable to process it. "This notice is for Li Luo?"

"Yeah, who else could it be for?" The courier gave Ying Zhicheng a slightly strange look. "The name is written right on it."

This came as quite a shock to Ying Zhicheng.

In his memory, this kid Li Luo's grades weren't that great, were they?

During the New Year, when the two families had dinner together, he and Li Guohong had even talked about Li Luo's final exam scores.

He ranked 27th in his class, and his total score was more than one hundred and seventy points lower than Ying Chanxi's.

Could he get into First Affiliated High with grades like that?

Ying Zhicheng was baffled. He watched as Li Luo came out of his apartment, took out his student card, signed the delivery slip, and received the package.

After the courier left, Li Luo glanced at Ying Zhicheng's expression and decided not to go back inside. He stood right there in the hallway, tore open the package in his hands, and took out an admission notice.

Ying Zhicheng came over from across the hall and looked at the contents.

There were two things inside the admission notice package. One was a certificate-like congratulatory letter, congratulating student Li Luo on his successful admission to our school, blah blah blah.

Then there was a school notice, stating the start date of the term, as well as the items to bring and various points of attention.

"You did well on your high school entrance exam?" Ying Zhicheng asked. "First Affiliated High is not easy to get into."

"Yeah, I scored 555," Li Luo said. "Ranked 86th in the entire district. Not bad, I guess, but definitely no match for Ying Chanxi."

"That's still very impressive." Ying Zhicheng looked at Li Luo, suddenly feeling that this kid might not be as bad as he had thought. "Perfect. We'll celebrate this for you at dinner tonight too."

"Then thank you in advance, Uncle Ying."

The two of them returned to their respective apartments from the hallway.

Li Luo went back, took a shower, and then lay down on his bed to catch up on sleep.

When he woke up, it was already past three in the afternoon.

Normally at this time, he would have run next door to Ying Chanxi's study to borrow her computer and continue writing.

But with Ying Zhicheng there now, Li Luo decided against it.

Anyway, he still had a lot of stockpiled chapters, so there was no rush for a day or two. He would just take a break today.

With this thought, Li Luo rolled over in bed and heard the sound of raindrops tapping against the window.

He sat up and looked outside.

The rain was pouring, and the view through the window was blurry.

Li Luo opened the window and saw it was raining cats and dogs outside. It probably wouldn't stop anytime soon.

So he simply got out of bed, rummaged through the cabinet by the door, found three umbrellas, changed his shoes, and prepared to take them to his parents.

But just as he opened his door, the door to 402 across the hall also opened.

Ying Zhicheng walked out of his apartment, and when he bumped into Li Luo, he was clearly a bit stunned too.

"Uncle Ying, are you heading out?" Li Luo asked curiously as he walked downstairs.

"Yeah, we're out of soy sauce at home. I forgot to buy it when I was grocery shopping," Ying Zhicheng said. "I have to go down and buy a bottle."

"I see." Li Luo stopped in his tracks and said to Ying Zhicheng, "Then you don't have to go down, Uncle Ying."

"I'm on my way to bring umbrellas to my parents. I can grab a bottle for you on my way back."

"It's pouring outside, no need for both of us to go down."

Hearing him say this, Ying Zhicheng nodded readily. "Then I'll have to trouble you."

"No trouble at all." Li Luo smiled and turned to run downstairs.

Watching Li Luo's departing back, Ying Zhicheng felt a bit dazed, with a sense that this kid, Li Luo, seemed to have suddenly become more steady and mature.

He wasn't as reckless and impatient as before.

With this thought, Ying Zhicheng turned and went back inside, continuing to prep the ingredients in the kitchen.

Li Luo, meanwhile, went downstairs, opened an umbrella, and plunged into the curtain of rain, heading for the breakfast shop across the street.

"Mom, I've left the umbrellas here! Remember to use them when you come home." Walking into the shop, Li Luo placed the two umbrellas in his hand on the counter and said to Lin Xiuhong.

Seeing her son had really come to deliver umbrellas, Lin Xiuhong's heart instantly warmed. "Got it."

"I'll head back then," Li Luo said. "Uncle Ying next door is back. He said he's cooking a meal and invited us over tonight."

"Yeah, your dad told me," Lin Xiuhong nodded, then didn't forget to add a reminder. "Remember not to tell Xixi, okay? Your Uncle Ying probably wants to give her a surprise. He didn't even tell her in advance."

"Oh?" Li Luo raised his eyebrows, then smiled. "Got it, I'll definitely keep it a secret."

After speaking, Li Luo opened his umbrella again, ran to the entrance of the residential complex across the street, bought a bottle of soy sauce at the supermarket, and then walked all the way back to the stairwell.

Closing his umbrella and climbing up to the fourth floor, Li Luo came to the door of 402 and subconsciously wanted to fish out the key from behind the couplet.

After a moment's thought, he pulled his hand back and knocked on the door instead.

A short while later, Ying Zhicheng came to open the door. After taking the soy sauce from Li Luo, he said to him, "Come in and sit. The computer in the study is free, you can go play for a bit."

Since Ying Zhicheng had said so, Li Luo, who had originally intended to go back to his own apartment, didn't stand on ceremony with him and walked inside to change into slippers.

Seeing him go back into the kitchen to continue his work, Li Luo wandered into the study, unceremoniously turned on the computer, logged into Qidian Chinese Website, and glanced at the Sanjiang recommendations list.

'I'm Really Not a Superstar' was impressively on it.

He had asked his editor yesterday, and his book's current number of concurrent readers was around 1200.

Once this round of recommendations was over, he could prepare to put the book up for sale next week.

Seeing his book's statistics, Li Luo could only shake his head and chuckle, thinking that if these numbers were from ten years later, forget Sanjiang, it would be a question whether it could even pass the third round of recommendations.

But Li Luo wasn't in a hurry. He knew very well where his advantages lay.

Right now, in 2014, the web novel industry was ushering in a new stage of development.

With the gradual popularization of smartphones, Qidian Chinese Website also followed the trend and launched the Qidian Reading App, joining the tidal wave of the mobile internet era.

By the end of the year, the distribution of Qidian's readership between desktop and mobile would already be an even fifty-fifty split.

By the end of '15, mobile users would account for 70%, and by the end of '16, this figure would swell to 90%.

Some people might think, what's the difference?

It's all just reading books. What's the difference between using a computer and a phone? At most, it's just more convenient to read novels on a phone.

But in fact, there were two very significant changes.

One was the change in the user base.

In the past, people who had access to a computer to go online and specifically read novels more or less had some level of education and literary appreciation. At the very least, they could learn how to use a computer, and their family's financial situation wouldn't be too bad.

But with the influx of smartphones, especially very cheap ones like Xiaomi, into the market, a population that had previously been cut off from the internet was suddenly absorbed into the mobile internet.

These users, at least in terms of literary appreciation and aesthetics, certainly didn't have such high demands as the previous user base.

Naturally, this would also lead to the rise of a batch of works that were more straightforward and gratifying.

The second was the change in the way people read.

Previously, when reading a novel on a computer, it was normal for an author to write a paragraph of several hundred words, and the layout on a computer screen was fine.

But the same paragraph, once placed on a mobile phone screen, would instantly become a huge, jumbled mess of text.

The reading experience would be extremely poor.

Many authors didn't realize this at first and still maintained their writing habits from the desktop era.

But for the new mobile users entering the world of web novels, if the text formatting issue could be solved, that book would have a head start right from the beginning.

Li Luo stood at the forefront of this tidal wave. His new book perfectly adapted to the changes of this phase, so it was only natural that he could achieve good results.

However, just as Li Luo was about to write a little, a sound came from the kitchen.

Puzzled, Li Luo walked out of the study and looked toward the kitchen, only to see Ying Zhicheng frowning, his right hand tightly clutching the fingers of his left hand.

Looking at the floor, a kitchen knife lay there, unclear how it had fallen.

"Uncle Ying, what's wrong?"

"Ngh... Hiss..." Ying Zhicheng's brow furrowed tightly as he sucked in a sharp breath. He looked at Li Luo and said with some helplessness, "I cut my hand while chopping vegetables."
